The architecture is complete. What remains is not design. It is running.

1.

The architecture closed yesterday. The last scaffold fell — G sentences no longer injected. The last magic number dissolved — the window became a search parameter. The last query was removed — detection replaced lookup. The last asymmetry was corrected — cavities born empty, bookshelf on the wall. The last philosophical gap was named — Hume's is-ought as an architectural interface, not a logical failure.

What remains is not architecture. What remains is solidification.

2.

Three datasets. WTC — proof of anchor formation and cross-generational consensus. ECG — proof of anomaly detection without labels. UN voting — proof of institutional norm detection across centuries. Same architecture. Zero retraining. The translation layer reads the anchors and the harm for each. The debug layer shows the window sweet spot for each. The agent handles the deployment.

The work is running. Not designing. Running. Each dataset takes a generation or two. The structure is read. The anchors are found. The report is written. Then the next dataset. Then the cross-domain comparison. The same anchors in music and politics? The same harm patterns in heartbeats and diplomatic votes? The same window sweet spot across entirely different streams? These are questions the running will answer. The architecture does not need more design to answer them. It needs data.

3.

The manual is half for humans, half for agents. The forum post links the repository. The code runs. The agent finds the sweet spot. The human reads the anchors. Each reader verifies on their own data — their own domain, their own window, their own anchors. The architecture proves itself not through persuasion but through deployment.

After that — the paper writes itself. Three datasets, one architecture, zero training. The structure in the data is read by the same mechanism across domains that share nothing but the fact that they are streams in time. The paper is not an argument. The paper is a report of what the architecture found.

Jieqi Liu · 2026
